There are four uniform colorings related to this tiling, corresponding to different subgroup symmetries. The dual tiling is known as the deltoidal trioctagonal tiling, which consists of kite-shaped faces. Each kite face corresponds to a vertex of the original rhombitrioctagonal tiling.

Like other hyperbolic semiregular tilings, the rhombitrioctagonal tiling cannot be realized in the Euclidean plane, as the vertex angles of the regular polygons meeting at each vertex exceed 360 degrees. Instead, it exists naturally on surfaces with constant negative curvature. The tiling is part of a broader family of rhombitriangular tilings, where similar constructions can be performed for other values.

In geometry, the rhombitrioctagonal tiling is a semiregular tiling of the 
hyperbolic plane. At each vertex of the tiling there is one triangle and one octagon, alternating between two squares. The tiling has Schläfli symbol rr{8,3}. It can be seen as constructed as a rectified trioctagonal tiling, r{8,3}, as well as an expanded octagonal tiling or expanded order-8 triangular tiling.

Symmetry 
This tiling has [8,3], (*832) symmetry.
